newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK, CZECH PMS TO MEET, BUT NOT OVER PROPERTY.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK, CZECH PMS TO MEET, BUT NOT OVER PROPERTY.

text.p: Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar will meet his Czech counterpart Vaclav Klaus on Friday but not to discuss senistive property issues from the breakup of Czechoslovakia, a Meciar aide said.
"The two will discuss general bilateral questions, but will not go into detail in this brief meeting," Meciar's spokeswoman Magda Pospisilova told Reuters.

The spokeswoman denied reports in the Czech and Slovak press that the two would discuss controversial open questions of property settlements stemming from the split-up of Czechoslovakia at the beginning of 1993.
"This is untrue, no such subject is on the agenda," Pospisilova said.
The Czechs and Slovaks have yet settle numerous divorce issues such as the divsion of federal gold reserves and cultural artifacts, and cross ownership of some banks.

However she said the Czech side had requested a second bilateral meeting, within the framework of the summit of the Central European Free Trade Agreement, which is taking place in the Slovak ski resort of Jasna on Friday and Saturday.
"But I don't know at present if that (second) meeting will take place," Pospisilova said.
This is Klaus's first visit to Slovakia since the breakup and Friday's meeting will be the first bilateral session between the two prime ministers in over a year.
The CEFTA meeting is to review progress in liberalising trade within the grouping, which consists of Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Slovenia.
A series of bilateral meetings, including those with representatives of CEFTA associate members Romania, Bulgaria, Ukraine, Lithuania and Latvia are scheduled over the next two days.
Slovakia currently holds the rotating presidency of CEFTA, which will go to Slovenia from next January. -- Peter Javurek, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-210-3587
